name: The Ritz-Carlton, Bali
positioning: Clifftop and beachside resort in Nusa Dua with private-pool villas, Indonesian dining and a sea-inspired spa
best_for: Families who want a free kids club
Couples who want a villa with a private pool

facts.text: The resort sits in Nusa Dua on a clifftop and beachside setting.
The Villa Collection villas were designed by Burega Farnell.
The floating breakfast is for in-house guests and costs extra.
Balinese Buffet Night is held every Saturday at Bejana.
Senses is a beachfront restaurant whose breakfast buffet spans Western, Chinese, Japanese, Indonesian and Indian dishes.
Spa treatments use natural ingredients of the beach and ocean, including pearls and seaweed.
The Yoga Studio offers a daily schedule of complimentary classes for all levels.
Children aged 4 to 12 can join Ritz Kids without a parent.
The Ritz Kids program is free and needs no reservation.

highlights.text: A floating breakfast is offered to guests in villas or suites with pool or lagoon access.
Bejana by Petty Elliott serves Indonesian cuisine and hosts cooking classes at the Culinary Cave.
The Balinese soul purification ritual, Melukat, takes place on the resort's beach in the early morning.
The spa's Hydro-Vital Pool has hydrotherapy zones that each target a different area of the body.
The resort partners with the Bali Sea Turtle Society to protect hatching sea turtles.

considerations.text: From the lobby it is about a 10-minute walk down to the water.
The nearest airport, Ngurah Rai International (DPS), is approximately 16.8 km from the hotel.
The sea turtle release program is seasonal, so guests should check availability.
